> Intended to assist a human reviewer, not replace one — suggestions may be
> incorrect, please verify before acting.


Adds GET /agents/{system_id}/dhcp-data exposing DHCPService.get_kea_dhcp_data_for_agent behind the existing internal client-cert middleware. Wiring verified end-to-end: ServiceCollectionV3.dhcp exists (src/maasservicelayer/services/__init__.py:279), the service raises the NotFoundException/ValidationException the tests mock, the global ExceptionMiddleware maps them to 404/422 (src/maasapiserver/common/middlewares/exceptions.py:129-134), and RequireClientCertMiddleware protects the new route (only /agents:enroll POST is skipped, src/maasapiserver/v3/middlewares/client_certificate.py:29-34). The response model embeds the maasservicelayer stdlib dataclasses directly — Pydantic v2 validates/serializes stdlib dataclasses so this works, but it is the first v3 response to do so (AgentResponse embeds a Pydantic model); see inline notes. Tests cover 200/403/404/422. Minor gaps: ipranges is never asserted, from_model's 1:1 field copy can silently drop new DHCPDataForAgent fields, and the two TLS test middlewares are near-duplicates. Pre-existing, out of diff scope: AgentConfigResponse.kind defaults to "AgentSignedCertificate", identical to AgentSignedCertificateResponse (responses/agent.py:45,100) — looks like a copy-paste oddity worth a follow-up.

src/maasapiserver/v3/api/internal/handle.200: RequireClientCertMiddleware (src/maasapiserver/v3/middlewares/client_certificate.py:38-45) returns 403 for any request without a client CN, but 403 isn't declared in `responses` even though ForbiddenBodyResponse already exists. /agents/{uuid}/config has the same gap, so this is consistent — but declaring `403: {"model": ForbiddenBodyResponse}` here (and ideally on the sibling) would make the generated OpenAPI accurate for agent clients.
src/maasapiserver/v3/api/internal/handle.212: Authz relies entirely on the global middleware: the client CN is only checked for presence, never bound to the requested `system_id`, so any agent holding a valid CA-issued client certificate can read any rack's DHCP topology (subnets, HA peer rack IPs, DNS/NTP servers). This matches /agents/{uuid}/config (which exposes rpc_secret the same way), so it presumably fits the internal threat model — flagging because this endpoint exposes more network-topology detail; worth an explicit decision whether CN→rack binding is expected.

src/maasapiserver/v3/api/internal/models.73: First v3 response model to embed raw stdlib dataclasses from maasservicelayer.models.dhcp; existing responses embed Pydantic models (e.g. AgentResponse/Agent). Pydantic v2 handles stdlib dataclasses, so this works, but the wire format then has no Pydantic-level constraints. If these DTOs are response-bound only, Pydantic models (or pydantic.dataclasses) would keep the response layer consistent; otherwise fine.
src/maasapiserver/v3/api/internal/models.85: This is a 1:1 copy of DHCPDataForAgent's seven fields; a future field added to DHCPDataForAgent won't appear in the response until both this model and from_model are updated, and nothing fails loudly. Deriving the copy from dataclasses.fields(dhcp_data), or adding a test that compares the two field sets, would keep them in sync.

src/tests/maasapiserver/v3/api/internal/.87: This ~60-line DHCP_DATA overlaps with the one in src/tests/maasapiserver/v3/api/internal/models/responses/test_agent.py:44. Fine for now, but if a third consumer appears consider a shared builder/fixture under tests/maasapiserver/fixtures.
src/tests/maasapiserver/v3/api/internal/.161: Duplicates InjectFakeTLSCN except for the tls dict contents; a single middleware taking client_cn (used as add_middleware(InjectFakeTLSCN, client_cn=None)) would cover both the with-cert and without-cert cases.
src/tests/maasapiserver/v3/api/internal/.340: ipranges is populated in DHCP_DATA and part of AgentDHCPDataResponse, but never asserted in either this test or the response-model test — a copy mistake in from_model would pass unnoticed. Add e.g. assert response_json["ipranges"] == [{"id": 1, "subnet_id": 1, "dynamic": True, "start_ip": "10.0.0.100", "end_ip": "10.0.0.200"}].
src/tests/maasapiserver/v3/api/internal/.423: Only the status code is asserted. Asserting the detail message too (response.json()["details"][0]["message"] == "The rack controller has no current configuration.") would pin that this is the rack-not-configured 422 rather than any validation failure.
